collections.name: Light & Landscape
collections.description: Films where the image carries the story. Start here for DPs and photographers.

collections.name: Interior Lives
collections.description: Films driven by writing and performance.

collections.name: Truth & Archive
collections.description: Documentaries that invent new forms for real stories.

collections.name: Foundations
collections.description: The classics every film here descends from.

collections.name: Netflix South Africa
collections.description: The commercial end of the industry, where Creative Directors are most likely to land work.

collections.name: The studio era
collections.description: 1927 to 1959: the studios' stars, sets and storytelling at their height.

collections.name: New Hollywood
collections.description: 1960 to 1979: directors break the old rules, on location and in colour.

collections.name: Modern classics
collections.description: 1985 to 1999: the films that shaped how the industry makes and sells films today.

collections.name: Black and POC leads
collections.description: Films led by Black, Asian and Latino stars, from The Emperor Jones to Black Panther.

titles.title: Mami Wata
titles.recognition: Sundance 2023, Special Jury Award for Cinematography
titles.study_note: High-contrast black and white by Lílis Soares; lighting dark skin against water and night

titles.title: This Is Not a Burial, It's a Resurrection
titles.recognition: Sundance 2020, Special Jury Award for Visionary Filmmaking; 31 wins and 12 nominations
titles.study_note: Painterly tableaux by Pierre de Villiers; Mary Twala's final lead role

titles.title: Timbuktu
titles.recognition: Cannes Competition 2014; 7 Césars incl. Best Film; Oscar nominee
titles.study_note: Desert compositions by Sofian El Fani; violence held at a distance

titles.title: Atlantics
titles.recognition: Cannes 2019 Grand Prix
titles.pair_with: Portrait of a Lady on Fire (Sciamma)
titles.study_note: Same DP, Claire Mathon: compare how she shoots the ocean and firelight in both

titles.title: Banel & Adama
titles.recognition: Cannes Competition 2023 (debut feature)
titles.study_note: Saturated color and landscape as fate, shot by Amine Berrada

titles.title: Sew the Winter to My Skin
titles.recognition: TIFF 2018; South Africa's Oscar submission
titles.study_note: Near-wordless storytelling; epic Karoo widescreen

titles.title: Five Fingers for Marseilles
titles.recognition: TIFF 2017, Discovery
titles.study_note: The western rebuilt in the Eastern Cape; frontier light

titles.title: Neptune Frost
titles.recognition: Cannes Directors' Fortnight 2021
titles.study_note: Afrofuturist musical; production design from recycled tech

titles.title: On Becoming a Guinea Fowl
titles.recognition: Cannes Un Certain Regard 2024, Best Director
titles.study_note: A family funeral exposes buried abuse; tone that shifts from comic to devastating

titles.title: I Am Not a Witch
titles.recognition: Cannes Directors' Fortnight 2017; BAFTA Outstanding Debut
titles.study_note: Same DP, David Gallego; satire built from stillness

titles.title: Goodbye Julia
titles.recognition: Cannes Un Certain Regard 2023, Freedom Prize
titles.study_note: A lie between two women set against Sudan's split; chamber-drama writing

titles.title: Lingui, The Sacred Bonds
titles.recognition: Cannes Competition 2021
titles.study_note: A mother and daughter navigating an abortion ban; restraint as tension

titles.title: Félicité
titles.recognition: Berlinale 2017 Silver Bear Grand Jury Prize; FESPACO Étalon d'or
titles.study_note: Kinshasa at night, shot by Céline Bozon; music as inner voice

titles.title: Eyimofe (This Is My Desire)
titles.recognition: Berlinale Forum 2020; Criterion Collection
titles.study_note: Two Lagos lives in parallel, on 16mm by Arseni Khachaturan

titles.title: Inxeba (The Wound)
titles.recognition: Sundance and Berlinale 2017; Oscar shortlist
titles.study_note: Masculinity and initiation; Nakhane's lead performance

titles.title: Rafiki
titles.recognition: Cannes Un Certain Regard 2018
titles.study_note: Pop color as defiance, shot by Christopher Wessels; a love story banned at home

titles.title: Feathers
titles.recognition: Cannes Critics' Week 2021, Grand Prize
titles.study_note: Deadpan absurdism; fixed frames and non-professional actors

titles.title: Heart of the Hunter
titles.recognition: First African film to reach No. 1 on Netflix's global Top 10
titles.study_note: Action thriller from Deon Meyer's novel; Western Cape vistas; a director with a cinematographer's eye

titles.title: Saloum
titles.recognition: TIFF 2021, Midnight Madness
titles.study_note: Mercenary thriller that turns supernatural; genre switching mid-film

titles.title: Hounds (Les Meutes)
titles.recognition: Cannes Un Certain Regard 2023, Jury Prize
titles.study_note: One night in Casablanca's underworld; handheld, real locations, shot by Amine Berrada

titles.title: Anikulapo
titles.recognition: 5 AMVCA wins incl. Best Movie in Africa
titles.study_note: Yoruba folklore epic; costume and period production design

titles.title: The Burial of Kojo
titles.recognition: Urbanworld 2018, Best Narrative Feature; Netflix via ARRAY
titles.study_note: Magical realism through a child's eyes; dreamlike color

titles.title: Children of Blood and Bone
titles.recognition: Upcoming: theatres and IMAX 15 January 2027
titles.study_note: Studio-scale fantasy world-building from West African-inspired myth; South African lead Thuso Mbedu with Damson Idris and Amandla Stenberg

titles.title: Blood & Water
titles.recognition: One of Netflix's most-watched African originals; SAFTA wins incl. cinematography
titles.study_note: Teen mystery with a trafficking thread; Cape Town as a character. Stars Ama Qamata, Khosi Ngema, Gail Mabalane

titles.title: The Polygamist
titles.recognition: Netflix Top 10 in South Africa within 24 hours; charted globally
titles.study_note: 22-episode adaptation of Sue Nyathi's novel; opens at a funeral and works backward. Stars S'dumo Mtshali, Gugu Gumede

titles.title: Shaka iLembe
titles.study_note: Period epic on the rise of Shaka Zulu; scale of costume, set and battle production

titles.title: DAM
titles.study_note: A young woman returns to her small hometown and confronts a buried past; dread built through landscape and sound

titles.title: Dahomey
titles.recognition: Berlinale 2024 Golden Bear
titles.study_note: Looted Beninese artefacts returned home; one artefact narrates

titles.title: Four Daughters
titles.recognition: Cannes 2023, L'Œil d'or; Oscar nominee
titles.study_note: Actors and real family members restage the past together

titles.title: The Mother of All Lies
titles.recognition: Cannes Un Certain Regard 2023, Best Director; Oscar shortlist
titles.study_note: Family memory rebuilt with handmade miniatures

titles.title: Touki Bouki
titles.recognition: Cannes 1973, FIPRESCI Prize; restored by the World Cinema Project
titles.study_note: Jump cuts and collage editing; the road movie made African

titles.title: Black Girl (La Noire de…)
titles.recognition: Prix Jean Vigo 1966
titles.study_note: Domestic labor and alienation; the first feature by a sub-Saharan African director

titles.title: Pumzi
titles.recognition: Sundance 2010, short films
titles.study_note: Afrofuturism on a small budget; 21 minutes of world-building

titles.title: How to Ruin Christmas
titles.study_note: Family farce built around a wedding, a funeral and a baby; ensemble comedy timing

titles.title: How to Ruin Love
titles.study_note: Two families' clashing traditions; Season 2 centres on lobola. Stars Sivenathi Mabuya

titles.title: Fatal Seduction
titles.study_note: Erotic thriller where an affair spirals into a murder investigation

titles.title: iNumber Number
titles.study_note: Johannesburg heist thriller; undercover cops crossing the line. Stars S'dumo Mtshali

titles.title: iNumber Number: Jozi Gold
titles.study_note: The Netflix sequel: a second Johannesburg heist with S'dumo Mtshali returning

titles.title: Go!
titles.study_note: A teen sprinter on a private-school scholarship hiding a fatal secret; sport plus social realism

titles.title: Umthetho
titles.study_note: Zulu-language crime drama: a state prosecutor becomes a double agent in her imprisoned brother's gang to keep their youngest brother alive. Stars Nqobile Nunu K.H., Given Stuurman, Tony Kgoroge

titles.title: Silverton Siege
titles.study_note: Apartheid-era bank siege inspired by real 1980 events

titles.title: Queen Sono
titles.study_note: Pan-African spy thriller led by Pearl Thusi

titles.title: Kings of Jo'burg
titles.study_note: Crime-family drama in Johannesburg with supernatural undertones

titles.title: Shadow
titles.study_note: South Africa's first Netflix original series; a vigilante who cannot feel pain

titles.title: Seriously Single
titles.study_note: Joburg rom-com about modern dating; sequel Seriously Single Too now streaming

titles.title: Savage Beauty
titles.study_note: Revenge thriller inside a cosmetics empire

titles.title: Kandasamys: The Baby
titles.study_note: Durban family comedy franchise; shot in South Africa and Mauritius

titles.title: The Brave Ones
titles.study_note: Supernatural revenge drama drawing on ancestral myth

titles.title: Unseen
titles.study_note: A cleaner searching for her missing husband reveals a dangerous past. Stars Gail Mabalane

titles.title: Marked
titles.pair_with: The Polygamist (same lead actor and showrunner)
titles.study_note: Stars S'dumo Mtshali; season 2 in production

titles.title: Lobola Man
titles.study_note: Rom-com about Ace Ngubeni, a slick lobola negotiator facing his toughest deal for a shy client; tradition as comic engine

titles.title: The Heart Is a Muscle
titles.recognition: Berlinale 2025, Panorama; South Africa's entry for the 98th Academy Awards
titles.study_note: A father's violent search for his missing son, and the masculinity that drives it; Imran Hamdulay's debut feature

titles.title: Gangster's Paradise: Jerusalema
titles.recognition: Berlinale 2008, Panorama; South Africa's entry for the 81st Academy Awards
titles.study_note: Hillbrow's building hijacks seen from the inside, inspired by true events; Johannesburg's 1990s on a crime-epic scale

titles.title: Nickel Boys
titles.recognition: Academy Award nominee, Best Picture and Best Adapted Screenplay; premiered at Telluride 2024
titles.study_note: Colson Whitehead's novel shot almost entirely in first person by Jomo Fray: the camera is the boys' eyes

titles.title: Capernaum
titles.recognition: Cannes 2018 Jury Prize; Academy Award nominee, Best Foreign Language Film
titles.study_note: A non-professional cast found on Beirut's streets, filmed at a child's eye level over months to catch real behaviour

titles.title: The Wizard of Oz
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Original Song and Best Original Score
titles.study_note: Sepia Kansas gives way to three-strip Technicolor Oz: colour as the story's turning point

titles.title: Citizen Kane
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay
titles.pair_with: The Mother of All Lies (El Moudir)
titles.study_note: Gregg Toland's deep focus and low angles; a life pieced together from other people's memories
titles.essential: It topped Sight and Sound's critics' poll for 50 years: the shorthand for an ambitious debut and for deep-focus craft.

titles.title: The Maltese Falcon
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Hard-boiled dialogue and low-key light that set the pattern for film noir

titles.title: Casablanca
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Picture, Director and Screenplay
titles.study_note: A studio-built Morocco, shadowed close-ups and a script rewritten during the shoot
titles.essential: The model studio-system picture: written while it was shot, endlessly quoted, still the reference for romance on screen.

titles.title: It's a Wonderful Life
titles.recognition: Five Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: A whole town's life told in flashback, on a snowbound set built for a summer shoot

titles.title: All About Eve
titles.recognition: Six Academy Awards from 14 nominations, including Best Picture and Director
titles.study_note: A backstage rivalry carried by dialogue and several voice-over narrators

titles.title: Sunset Boulevard
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Story and Screenplay
titles.study_note: Hollywood looking at itself: a dead narrator, a forgotten silent star and a decaying mansion
titles.essential: Hollywood's own warning about fame and the studio machine; its last line is one of the most quoted.

titles.title: Singin' in the Rain
titles.recognition: Two Academy Award nominations
titles.study_note: Dance staged for the camera; the move from silent films to sound played as comedy
titles.essential: The industry laughing at itself over the arrival of sound: the musical everyone in the room has seen.

titles.title: Roman Holiday
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Actress (Audrey Hepburn) and Best Story
titles.study_note: Shot on location in Rome, rare for a studio picture of its time

titles.title: On the Waterfront
titles.recognition: Eight Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Director and Actor (Marlon Brando)
titles.study_note: Method acting on the real Hoboken docks; the taxi-cab scene

titles.title: Carmen Jones
titles.recognition: Dorothy Dandridge became the first Black woman nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress
titles.study_note: Bizet's opera reset with an all-Black cast, in CinemaScope colour

titles.title: Rebel Without a Cause
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations
titles.study_note: Wide CinemaScope colour turned on teenage anguish; James Dean's defining role

titles.title: The Searchers
titles.recognition: Named the greatest American western by the American Film Institute (2008)
titles.study_note: Monument Valley in VistaVision; the doorway shots that open and close the film

titles.title: Vertigo
titles.recognition: Voted the greatest film of all time in Sight and Sound's 2012 critics' poll
titles.study_note: The dolly zoom; colour, especially green, as obsession; Saul Bass's titles
titles.essential: It replaced Citizen Kane at the top of Sight and Sound's poll in 2012: the film people mean when they talk about Hitchcock's craft.

titles.title: Some Like It Hot
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Costume Design
titles.study_note: Shot in black and white so the drag make-up would read; comic timing held in long takes

titles.title: Imitation of Life
titles.recognition: Academy Award nominations for Juanita Moore and Susan Kohner
titles.study_note: Melodrama as social critique: colour, mirrors and a funeral finale

titles.title: Psycho
titles.recognition: Four Academy Award nominations
titles.study_note: Killing off the star halfway through; the shower scene's rapid cutting and Bernard Herrmann's strings
titles.essential: Made cheaply with a TV crew and sold with a no-late-admission rule: proof that marketing and craft can turn a small film into an event.

titles.title: West Side Story
titles.recognition: Ten Academy Awards, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Gang conflict as dance on real New York streets; colour-coded light

titles.title: Lawrence of Arabia
titles.recognition: Seven Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Director
titles.study_note: Desert vistas in Super Panavision 70; the cut from a blown-out match to the sunrise

titles.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Actor (Gregory Peck) and Adapted Screenplay
titles.study_note: A novel adapted through a child's eyes; the courtroom as the film's moral centre

titles.title: In the Heat of the Night
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Picture and Best Actor (Rod Steiger)
titles.study_note: Racial tension built into a murder procedural; Haskell Wexler's lighting for Sidney Poitier

titles.title: The Graduate
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Director
titles.study_note: Long lenses that trap Benjamin in the frame; Simon & Garfunkel songs as narration

titles.title: Bonnie and Clyde
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Supporting Actress (Estelle Parsons) and Cinematography
titles.study_note: New Hollywood's break with the old code: violence, sex and abrupt editing

titles.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Visual Effects
titles.study_note: Front projection, practical effects and long silences; the bone-to-satellite match cut
titles.essential: The reference point for practical visual effects and for trusting an audience with silence.

titles.title: The Godfather
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Picture, Actor (Marlon Brando) and Adapted Screenplay
titles.study_note: Gordon Willis's top-lit darkness; the baptism cross-cut with the killings
titles.essential: The yardstick for adaptation and ensemble casting, and for the fight between a director and his studio that New Hollywood was made of.

titles.title: Jaws
titles.recognition: Three Academy Awards (editing, score and sound); the first summer blockbuster
titles.study_note: A broken mechanical shark turned into suspense: the threat mostly unseen, John Williams's two notes
titles.essential: It invented the summer blockbuster: a wide release backed by national TV advertising, the plan most tentpole releases still follow.

titles.title: Taxi Driver
titles.recognition: Palme d'Or, Cannes 1976
titles.study_note: New York at night through a disturbed narrator; Bernard Herrmann's last score

titles.title: Network
titles.recognition: Four Academy Awards, three of them for acting
titles.study_note: Paddy Chayefsky's satire of television, delivered in long, theatrical speeches
titles.essential: Its predictions about television news are quoted in every conversation about media; 'mad as hell' is part of the vocabulary.

titles.title: Star Wars
titles.recognition: Six Academy Awards
titles.study_note: A lived-in, used-future world built from models, production design and sound design
titles.essential: George Lucas kept the sequel and merchandising rights: it turned merchandise into the business model and changed how deals are made.

titles.title: Apocalypse Now
titles.recognition: Palme d'Or, Cannes 1979
titles.pair_with: Sew the Winter to My Skin (Qubeka)
titles.study_note: A troubled shoot in the Philippines; Vittorio Storaro's colour and Walter Murch's sound design
titles.essential: The cautionary tale of a shoot running out of control, retold in the documentary Hearts of Darkness.

titles.title: Ride Along
titles.recognition: Number one at the US box office on its opening weekend
titles.study_note: Buddy-comedy chemistry between Ice Cube and Kevin Hart; comic timing inside action set pieces

titles.title: The Matrix
titles.recognition: Four Academy Awards, including Best Visual Effects
titles.study_note: Bullet time, Yuen Woo-ping's wire-work fights and a green-tinted digital world
titles.essential: Bullet time, the Wachowskis' world-building and a franchise blueprint: still the reference in action and visual-effects pitches.

titles.title: Coming to America
titles.recognition: Two Academy Award nominations (costume design and make-up)
titles.study_note: Eddie Murphy and Arsenio Hall in several roles each under Rick Baker's make-up

titles.title: Coming 2 America
titles.recognition: Academy Award nomination for Best Makeup and Hairstyling
titles.study_note: Ruth E. Carter's costumes bring Zamunda back in colour; a legacy sequel built on its returning cast

titles.title: The Karate Kid
titles.recognition: Over $350 million worldwide
titles.study_note: The remake moved to Beijing: Jackie Chan's dramatic turn and training scenes shot on location in China

titles.title: The Pursuit of Happyness
titles.recognition: Academy Award nomination for Best Actor (Will Smith)
titles.study_note: A true story played close to the ground; Will Smith opposite his son Jaden

titles.title: Do the Right Thing
titles.recognition: Academy Award nominations for Best Original Screenplay and Supporting Actor (Danny Aiello)
titles.study_note: Ernest Dickerson's heat-soaked colour, tilted angles and a single Brooklyn block
titles.essential: Spike Lee's breakthrough, on every list of essential American films; the reference for colour, heat and point of view.

titles.title: Boyz n the Hood
titles.recognition: John Singleton became the youngest person and the first Black director nominated for Best Director
titles.study_note: Coming of age in South Central Los Angeles; a debut written from life

titles.title: Malcolm X
titles.recognition: Academy Award nominations for Best Actor (Denzel Washington) and Costume Design
titles.study_note: A three-hour epic biopic: Ruth E. Carter's costumes and Denzel Washington's transformation

titles.title: Training Day
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Actor (Denzel Washington)
titles.study_note: One day in a car with a corrupt detective; Denzel Washington cast against type

titles.title: Ray
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Actor (Jamie Foxx)
titles.study_note: A music biopic built on Jamie Foxx's performance and Ray Charles's own recordings

titles.title: Dreamgirls
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress (Jennifer Hudson)
titles.study_note: A Broadway musical brought to the screen, with performances staged after the Motown era

titles.title: Bad Boys
titles.recognition: The start of a four-film franchise
titles.study_note: Will Smith and Martin Lawrence improvising inside glossy, fast-cut action

titles.title: Waiting to Exhale
titles.recognition: Adapted from Terry McMillan's best-selling novel
titles.study_note: Four friends' lives in parallel; an ensemble led by Whitney Houston and Angela Bassett

titles.title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon
titles.recognition: Four Academy Awards, including Best Foreign Language Film
titles.study_note: Yuen Woo-ping's wire-work; fights staged like dance in the bamboo treetops

titles.title: Get Out
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay
titles.study_note: Social horror built from everyday racism; the Sunken Place
titles.essential: A $4.5 million film that took over $250 million and won Best Original Screenplay: the model for genre with something to say.

titles.title: Black Panther
titles.recognition: Three Academy Awards (costume design, production design and score)
titles.study_note: Afrofuturist world-building: Ruth E. Carter's costumes and Hannah Beachler's production design
titles.essential: Over $1.3 billion worldwide and the first superhero film nominated for Best Picture: it ended the argument about Black-led blockbusters.

titles.title: Moonlight
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Picture
titles.study_note: One life in three chapters played by three actors; James Laxton's saturated Miami colour
titles.essential: A Best Picture winner made for about $4 million, and the envelope mix-up at the Oscars made it a story everyone tells.

titles.title: Hidden Figures
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: The true story of the Black women mathematicians behind NASA's early space flights

titles.title: Crazy Rich Asians
titles.recognition: The first major Hollywood studio film with a majority Asian cast in 25 years
titles.study_note: A romantic comedy staged as spectacle in Singapore; casting and costume as world-building

titles.title: Rocky
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Picture and Director
titles.study_note: Made for about $1 million; the training montage and the museum steps shot with an early Steadicam
titles.essential: Sylvester Stallone wouldn't sell his script unless he starred in it: the story every writer-actor hears about betting on yourself.

titles.title: The Godfather Part II
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Picture, Director and Supporting Actor (Robert De Niro)
titles.study_note: A sequel and a prequel cut together: two timelines in parallel
titles.essential: The first sequel to win Best Picture: the answer whenever someone says sequels can't be art.

titles.title: Back to the Future
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Sound Effects Editing
titles.study_note: Every scene sets up a payoff; Michael J. Fox replaced the original lead weeks into the shoot
titles.essential: Taught in screenwriting classes for its setups and payoffs: nothing on screen is wasted.

titles.title: Die Hard
titles.recognition: Four Academy Award nominations
titles.study_note: One building as the whole world; the hero as an ordinary man
titles.essential: 'Die Hard on a…' is how countless action films are pitched: the template for a contained, single-location thriller.

titles.title: Jurassic Park
titles.recognition: Three Academy Awards, including Best Visual Effects
titles.study_note: Stan Winston's animatronics alongside Industrial Light & Magic's computer-generated dinosaurs
titles.essential: The turning point from practical effects to computer-generated creatures, made by blending both.

titles.title: Pulp Fiction
titles.recognition: Palme d'Or, Cannes 1994, and the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay
titles.study_note: Chapters told out of order; long, dialogue-led scenes
titles.essential: Won the Palme d'Or and turned an independent film into a box-office hit: the reference for non-linear structure and dialogue.

titles.title: The Shawshank Redemption
titles.recognition: Seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Roger Deakins's restrained photography; a voice-over carrying a decades-long story
titles.essential: It disappointed at the box office, then became beloved on home video and TV: the case study for a film's second life.

titles.title: Toy Story
titles.recognition: A Special Achievement Academy Award as the first feature-length computer-animated film
titles.study_note: Characters designed around what computers could render; story first
titles.essential: The first fully computer-animated feature; its story-first process is still copied by studios.

titles.title: Titanic
titles.recognition: Eleven Academy Awards, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: A near-full-scale ship built in a tank in Mexico; spectacle carried by a love story
titles.essential: It ran far over budget with the industry predicting disaster, then became the highest-grossing film of its time.

titles.title: The Blair Witch Project
titles.recognition: Made for a reported $60,000; it earned about $248 million
titles.study_note: Found footage shot by the actors themselves; largely improvised performances
titles.essential: Sold through an early internet campaign that blurred fact and fiction: the case study in viral marketing.

titles.title: Gone with the Wind
titles.recognition: Eight Academy Awards, including Best Picture; Hattie McDaniel became the first Black actor to win an Oscar
titles.study_note: Technicolor at epic scale: firelit night scenes and burnt-orange skies. Study it with its romanticised view of slavery in mind
titles.essential: Still the biggest box-office film once prices are adjusted, and the reference point for Technicolor spectacle and for how Hollywood romanticised the Old South.

titles.title: Double Indemnity
titles.recognition: Seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: The film noir template: venetian-blind shadows, a voice-over confession and a scheme that goes wrong
titles.essential: The noir that crime writers and DPs still borrow from: told backwards from a confession and lit through venetian blinds.

titles.title: Rear Window
titles.recognition: Four Academy Award nominations, including Best Director
titles.study_note: One courtyard set and one point of view: suspense built from what the camera, and the audience, can see
titles.essential: Hitchcock's lesson in point of view and suspense, shot from one apartment on one enormous studio set.

titles.title: North by Northwest
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations
titles.study_note: The chase-film blueprint: a crop-duster attack in open daylight, Saul Bass's opening titles and a Mount Rushmore finale
titles.essential: The template for the spy chase film; the crop-duster scene is the reference for suspense in broad daylight.

titles.title: It Happened One Night
titles.recognition: The first film to win all five top Academy Awards: picture, director, actor, actress and screenplay
titles.study_note: The screwball road comedy: sparring leads, quick dialogue and a bus trip that turns into a romance
titles.essential: The first film to sweep the five top Oscars, and the template the romantic comedy still follows.

titles.title: The Grapes of Wrath
titles.recognition: Academy Awards for Best Director and Best Supporting Actress
titles.study_note: Gregg Toland's deep-focus black and white turns Dust Bowl migration into images that look like documentary photographs

titles.title: Mildred Pierce
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Actress (Joan Crawford)
titles.study_note: Noir lighting around a mother-and-daughter melodrama, told in flashback from a murder

titles.title: Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans
titles.recognition: Three Academy Awards at the first ceremony, including Unique and Artistic Production
titles.study_note: German expressionism inside a Hollywood studio: forced-perspective city sets, superimpositions and a camera that moves, with no dialogue

titles.title: Ben-Hur
titles.recognition: 11 Academy Awards, a record later matched by Titanic and The Return of the King
titles.study_note: The chariot race: months of second-unit work, a vast arena set and widescreen staging that action films still study
titles.essential: The chariot race is still the benchmark for practical action at scale, and its 11 Oscars are still the record.

titles.title: Paths of Glory
titles.recognition: Not shown in France until 1975
titles.study_note: Kubrick's long tracking shots through the trenches, set against a château where the generals decide who dies

titles.title: 12 Angry Men
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: One room, twelve actors, close to real time: the lenses get longer and the camera lower as the pressure rises
titles.essential: The model for drama in a single room: Lumet shoots it with longer lenses and a lower camera as the tension builds.

titles.title: City Lights
titles.study_note: Chaplin kept it silent after sound arrived: physical comedy, his own score and a final close-up that does the work of dialogue
titles.essential: Chaplin's silent comedy made after sound took over; its last close-up is taught as one of the great endings.

titles.title: Footlight Parade
titles.study_note: Busby Berkeley's overhead kaleidoscope numbers: choreography designed for the camera, not the stage

titles.title: Out of the Past
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1991
titles.study_note: Nicholas Musuraca's noir lighting and a flashback plot about a man who can't outrun his past

titles.title: Rebecca
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Picture, the only Hitchcock film to win it
titles.study_note: A house as the antagonist: a dead woman who never appears fills every room through the sets, the shadows and the housekeeper

titles.title: Seven Samurai
titles.recognition: Silver Lion at the Venice Film Festival
titles.study_note: Several cameras, long lenses, mud and rain: battle staged in weather, with the team gathered one man at a time
titles.essential: The source of the gather-the-team story, from The Magnificent Seven to heist films, and the reference for staging battle in weather.

titles.title: I Am a Fugitive from a Chain Gang
titles.recognition: Three Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture
titles.study_note: Warner Bros.' social realism before the Production Code: a true story that helped end the chain gangs, with a famously dark last line

titles.title: The Ox-Bow Incident
titles.recognition: Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture
titles.study_note: A western without heroes: a lynch mob over a single day, shot mostly on soundstages

titles.title: The Shop Around the Corner
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1999
titles.study_note: The Lubitsch touch: two shop clerks who can't stand each other are each other's pen pals, almost all on one shop set

titles.title: Trouble in Paradise
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1991
titles.study_note: Pre-Code sophistication: two thieves in love, told through doors, clocks and what the camera leaves out

titles.title: Stormy Weather
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 2001
titles.study_note: A studio musical with an all-Black cast built around Lena Horne, Bill Robinson and Cab Calloway; the Nicholas Brothers' stair-leaping finale is still studied by choreographers
titles.essential: The Nicholas Brothers' finale is one of the most referenced dance numbers ever filmed.

titles.title: Cabin in the Sky
titles.recognition: Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song
titles.study_note: Minnelli's first feature: an all-Black musical fable with Ethel Waters, Lena Horne and Louis Armstrong, made inside MGM's studio system

titles.title: The Emperor Jones
titles.study_note: Paul Robeson in Eugene O'Neill's play, billed above his white co-stars in 1933: the rise and fall of a Pullman porter who makes himself an island's ruler

titles.title: Porgy and Bess
titles.recognition: Academy Award for Best Scoring of a Musical Picture
titles.study_note: Goldwyn's widescreen Todd-AO version of the Gershwin opera with Sidney Poitier, Dorothy Dandridge and Sammy Davis Jr., rarely seen since the Gershwin estate withdrew it

titles.title: A Raisin in the Sun
titles.recognition: Gary Cooper Award at the Cannes Film Festival
titles.study_note: Lorraine Hansberry's play with most of its Broadway cast: a Chicago family in one cramped apartment, the drama built from close quarters
titles.essential: Lorraine Hansberry's story of a Black family's dream of a house is a cornerstone of American drama, and one of Sidney Poitier's defining roles.

titles.title: Imitation of Life (1934)
titles.recognition: Nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture
titles.study_note: The first version of Fannie Hurst's story, in which Louise Beavers' and Fredi Washington's storyline about race and passing outweighs the star's

titles.title: Lilies of the Field
titles.recognition: Sidney Poitier became the first Black man to win the Academy Award for Best Actor
titles.study_note: A small, warm film shot in about two weeks in Arizona, carried by Poitier and a handful of nuns
titles.essential: Sidney Poitier's Best Actor Oscar, the first for a Black man, is a landmark every history of the industry comes back to.

titles.title: The Blood of Jesus
titles.recognition: Added to the National Film Registry in 1991
titles.study_note: A race film made for a few thousand dollars with a Texas church congregation in the cast, and one of the most successful of its time

titles.title: Native Son (1951)
titles.study_note: Richard Wright plays Bigger Thomas in the film of his own novel, shot in Argentina when no US studio would make it as written

titles.title: The Joe Louis Story
titles.study_note: A boxing biopic that cuts Joe Louis's real fight footage into the drama, with Coley Wallace as Louis

categories.name: Made in Africa
categories.description: African film and series, curated for cinematography and writing.

categories.name: Explore all
categories.description: The broader Explore library: international titles outside Made in Africa.

categories.name: Hollywood Classics
categories.description: Hollywood's defining films, from the studio era to today.
